topic.title: Why does no country own Antarctica?
topic.map_answer: the slices seven countries drew on Antarctica, three of them overlapping on the peninsula, frozen by the 1959 treaty line south of 60 degrees, with one slice of the continent claimed by nobody

shape.name: The frozen slices
shape.beats: hook: the white continent cut into slices and the claim -> how big it is against places the viewer knows -> a year slider: each country draws its slice on its year, flag planted at the pole -> three slices overlap on the peninsula, the quarrel -> the turn: twelve nations sign in 1959 and every slice freezes -> what the treaty forbids, one thing on the map each -> how many countries have signed since -> payoff: the one slice nobody claims and the year the deal can be reviewed -> loop back to the sliced continent
shape.why: a why-shaped story whose answer is lines on the map: slices drawn year by year on a slider, then frozen in place by one treaty

title: Britain, Chile and Argentina all claim the same ice
description:
Antarctica is cut into slices on the map, so why does no country own it?
The claims drawn year by year, the overlap on the peninsula, and the treaty that froze every line.
Sources: Wikipedia, Antarctic Treaty System; Antarctic Treaty Secretariat (Nov 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
